NOTE: the leaderboard record (184320) omits computableWitness; reproduce its circuit shape on the valid baseline AND add a fully-proved computableWitness. GKR/sum-check results (<4k) are a DIFFERENT proof system and do not transfer to this R1CS metric.

COST DIAGNOSIS (derived — verify before trusting): the record 184320 = 1600 bits x 24 rounds x 4.8. The sibling GF(2) challenge does the SAME permutation shape at 2.0 per bit-round (1 allocation + 1 constraint = just chi's product). The whole 2.8/bit gap is XOR OVERHEAD: over the circom prime a XOR b = a + b - 2ab costs a MULTIPLICATION, whereas over GF(2) it is free addition. So the entire remaining win on this challenge is in how XOR is encoded — not in chi, whose multiplicative complexity is already minimal (5 per 5-bit row, SAT-proven).

SUM-THEN-EXTRACT-PARITY for wide XORs (the main lever): to XOR k bits over a large prime field, do NOT chain k-1 pairwise a+b-2ab products. Instead form S = b_1 + ... + b_k as a FREE affine combination (zero constraints), then extract S mod 2 by decomposing S into ceil(log2(k+1)) bits with one linear equation S = 2q + r; the parity bit r IS the XOR. Cost ~log2(k) allocations + booleanity instead of (k-1) multiplications. theta XORs 5 lane bits plus a rotated column parity (k~5-11), where log2 beats linear decisively — this is how theta becomes near-free in a NON-binary field.

FOLD BOOLEANITY INTO THE PRODUCT: if c = a*b with a,b already known boolean, c is automatically boolean — do NOT emit a separate c(c-1)=0 row. Likewise the parity bit from a sum-decomposition is forced boolean by the range argument. Every redundant booleanity row is a pure loss at 1 constraint each, and at 38400 chi outputs that is 38400 constraints if repeated.

DO-NOT-TRY, AND IT IS A TEMPTING ONE: XOR-GATE / SHORTEST-LINEAR-PROGRAM MINIMIZATION BUYS EXACTLY ZERO HERE. There is a large and still-active literature on minimizing the number of 2-input XOR gates needed to evaluate an F2-LINEAR MAP — the Shortest Linear Program problem: Boyar-Peralta, Tan-Peyrin (TCHES'20) adding randomization and 3-input XOR gates, the 'Superior Boyar-Peralta' (SBP) depth-aware heuristic, 'Improved Heuristics for Low-Latency Implementations of Linear Layers', and eprint 2025/1493 which revisits BP and cuts the AES linear layer from 91 to 89 g-XOR. Keccak's theta (and rho/pi, and SHA-256's Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1) are exactly such linear maps, so this looks like the obvious attack on the biggest remaining slack. IT IS NOT, BECAUSE AN XOR GATE COSTS NOTHING IN EITHER OF OUR COST MODELS. In native R1CS an affine combination lives inside the A/B/C vectors of a row and is free. In the GF(2) challenges the harness restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A and B AFFINE, so an arbitrary XOR-combination is free inside a multiplicand. Halving the XOR count of theta changes the score by ZERO. WHAT THETA'S 2240 ROWS PER ROUND ACTUALLY PAY FOR IS *MATERIALIZATION*, NOT XOR COUNT: a value costs an allocation exactly when it must appear as a BARE WITNESS VARIABLE — because it is a circuit output, or because its consumer needs a variable rather than an affine form. THEREFORE THE ONLY QUESTION WORTH ASKING IS: for each currently-materialized intermediate, WHO CONSUMES IT, and can that consumer take an affine form instead? Every row saved comes from deleting a materialization, never from restructuring the XOR tree that feeds it.
rsa-pkcs1v15-sha256-4096-65537: HEAD-TO-HEAD MODMUL COUNTS ACROSS FOUR CODEBASES, ALL COMPILED AND MEASURED IN OUR MODEL (no lookups, no challenges), for one 256-bit a*b mod p over BN254: jsnark/xJsnark with a CONSTANT modulus and lazy range = 623 constraints at 32-bit chunks; jsnark with a variable modulus = 637 at 26-bit; arkworks r1cs-std emulated_fp = 680 (66 for mul_without_reduce + 614 for reduce) at 17 limbs x 15 bits; gnark v0.8.1 = 724 at 26x10 and 888 at its shipped 64x4. LIMB WIDTH 26-32 IS OPTIMAL AND 64 IS 18-22% WORSE — measured independently in two different codebases, and it reproduces xJsnark's own Figure 5 parameter sweep (b about 32 near-optimal, b = 120 about 40% worse). WE USE 4 LIMBS OF 64 BITS, i.e. the worst end of that curve; this is the same conclusion the pseudo-Mersenne analysis reached from a different direction, so treat 32-bit limbs as strongly corroborated. STRUCTURE OF THE COST, which is why: product limbs hinted and verified at 2n-1 FIXED points costs 2n-1 rows (15 at w=32) and is essentially free; q*p is FREE when p is a compile-time constant since constant scalings are linear; grouped carry propagation is 60-110; and ABOUT 80% OF THE WHOLE THING is bit-decomposition range checks on the quotient and remainder. LAZY REDUCTION IS WORTH ABOUT 600 CONSTRAINTS PER AVOIDED REDUCE (arkworks measures mul_without_reduce at 66 against reduce at 614, and additions cost literally zero), so a*b + c*d with one shared reduction is about 746 against 1360. FINALLY, WHY GNARK'S HEADLINE 99 CONSTRAINTS PER EMULATED MUL IS NOT AVAILABLE: modern gnark's mulMod emits ZERO constraints and defers to a Schwartz-Zippel check at a commitment-derived challenge (std/math/emulated/field_mul.go), and std/multicommit panics outright if the frontend is not a Committer — so it cannot even compile on a plain Groth16 frontend. Strip the challenge and the lookups and gnark's own pre-v0.10 code lands at 724.

PARAMETER TUNING IS EXHAUSTED — FIVE LEVERS CHECKED AND CLOSED (independent cost model reproduced 326297 to within a few percent, so these numbers are trustworthy). (a) KARATSUBA/TOOM IS ALREADY SUBSUMED: checking the product by EVALUATION AT 2m-1 FIXED CONSTANT POINTS, sum x_i c^i * sum y_i c^i = sum z_i c^i, is Toom taken to the maximum, costs 2m-1 rows (Theta(m), below Karatsuba's m^1.58), and interpolation is linear hence FREE. Do not implement Karatsuba. (b) SQUARING SYMMETRY tri(m) = m(m+1)/2 IS WORTHLESS under that scheme — a(c)*a(c) is one row per point exactly like a(c)*b(c); tri(m) only matters in the witness generator. (c) 17 MULTIPLICATIONS IS PROVABLY OPTIMAL: a length-k addition chain reaches at most 2^k and 2^16 < 65537, so l(65537) >= 17; 16 squarings + 1 multiply attains it and windowing cannot help at Hamming weight 2. (d) MERGING SQUARINGS (deferring reduction across steps) IS STRICTLY WORSE: for x^4 in one step the quotient grows to 12288 bits and the total is 26302 bits against 18782 for two separate squarings. (e) LIMB WIDTH IS A FLAT OPTIMUM: the 2mb range-check term is invariant in b, so only the carry term (proportional to b) and the evaluation term (1/b) trade off; b=17 is best and beats our b=24 by only 0.9%. xJsnark found the same plateau.

WHERE THE COST ACTUALLY IS, AND WHY IT IS HARD TO MOVE: about 82% of each modmul is TWO 4096-bit range checks — the quotient q and the remainder r, roughly 8037 rows each at b=24 — with grouped carries about 2627 and the evaluation rows about 1364. THE OBVIOUS ATTACK FAILS FOR TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS. Dropping the quotient range check (letting the carry bounds force q small) is INCOMPATIBLE WITH GROUPED CARRIES: grouping bounds only the group sums, not the individual coefficients, so you would need one carry per coefficient — 12276 bits per op instead of 1368, a net loss of about 21800 against the 8037 saved. It is also UNSOUND for adversarial n: if every limb of n is even, take q0 = 1/2 mod p and every (q*n)_i is a 23-bit value, the carry chain passes, and the circuit accepts a*b - r = n/2. RNS/CRT is likewise dead in plain R1CS — reducing modulo an auxiliary prime needs a witnessed quotient of full bit length, costing at least what it saves; RNS only pays when range checks are lookups. Barrett vs Montgomery is irrelevant because the quotient is nondeterministic advice, so there is no division to optimise. AND THE RANGE CHECK ITSELF IS OPTIMAL: a k-bit check costs 2k-1 (k rows + k-1 allocations) and that is a lower bound — r rank-1 rows cut a variety whose projection has degree at most 2^r by Bezout, so at most 2^r values can be accepted. The top-bit-fold already attains it; base-4 or base-8 digit decompositions tie at best.

MEASURED STATE OF OUR OWN CIRCUIT, SO NOBODY RE-OPTIMISES WHAT IS DONE: PadDigest24 costs Count.zero — the PKCS#1 v1.5 padding check is ALREADY FREE, because the padded block is a constant plus a linear form in the digest bits and constants live in the linear combination (equality against a long CONSTANT is always free in R1CS; only equality between two ALLOCATED values costs a row). It witnesses just 14 split bits for the digest straddling limb boundaries. Remaining small levers, in order: range-check the BYTES rather than the limbs of the modulus and signature (512 x (2*8-1) = 7680 per array against 171 x (2*24-1) = 8037, saving about 357 each, and bytes < 256 implies limbs < 2^24); and b = 24 -> 17 for about 0.9%. CALIBRATION: circom-rsa-verify is 536212 constraints for RSA-2048 including SHA — three times worse at half the modulus size. No published R1CS count exists for RSA-4096 with the digest as an input, so 326297 may be the best number in existence for this problem. OPEN AND GENUINELY MOTIVATING: the accepted witness set is parameterised by (s, n) alone, about 2^8192 points, so the Bezout row lower bound for the whole circuit is only about 8192 rows — roughly 40x below the record. Nothing information-theoretic forbids a far cheaper circuit; it is only that every known way to pin a nondeterministic 4096-bit quotient costs one row per bit.

CORRECTION — THERE IS NO SHA-256 IN THIS CIRCUIT. Verified against the challenge interface: `digest : Vector F digestBytesLen` is an INPUT ('SHA-256 digest of the message being verified'), and the seed solution contains zero hash/compression files — every module is bigint machinery (SqMulModBal, ModExpSq, GroupedEq*, EqViaCarries, MixedRadix, Bytes*). The published '66% SHA-2 / 14% bigint' split for RS256 circuits does NOT apply here because those circuits hash the message and this one does not. ALL ~326k of the cost is non-native bigint arithmetic: the 16 squarings + 1 multiply mod a 4096-bit N, plus byte<->limb conversion and the padding comparison. Optimise the modmul and the limb/carry machinery; do not go looking for a hash to shrink.
Exponent 65537 = 2^16 + 1: exactly 16 squarings + 1 multiply; every step is a fixed-modulus modmul — share reduction machinery across all 17.
Fixed modulus: precompute q'[0] (Montgomery -N^{-1} mod 2^w), R^2 mod N, and all modulus limbs as circuit CONSTANTS — no in-circuit inverse or per-op setup.
CIOS/Montgomery with carry elimination: when the top modulus word is bounded ((D-1)/2-1), the t[N]/t[N+1] carries are provably zero, dropping ~5N+2 additions per multiply (gnark result).
Limb count sweet spot N<=12 wide limbs; minimize the number of carries that need range checks — each naive range check costs ~1/2 constraint per bit, so wider limbs with fewer carries win.
CRT / RNS residue representation to split the 4096-bit reduce into independent smaller-modulus channels; recombine once at the end.
Only range-check the modular residual, the quotient coefficient, and carries — not every intermediate; use top-bit-fold range checks.

LAZY REDUCTION with static limb-bound tracking (xJsnark long-integer arithmetic): carry a compile-time upper bound per limb and let partial products accumulate in wider limbs; emit a carry-normalization + range check ONLY when a limb's tracked bound would exceed field capacity, instead of normalizing after every op. Across the 16 squarings + 1 multiply this removes whole normalization passes, not just individual carries.

DEFERRAL BUDGET, concretely (circom-ecdsa): with n-bit limbs and k of them, unreduced accumulation is safe while 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < (native field bits). Use this inequality to place carry/reduce passes at the LAST legal moment instead of guessing; multiples of the fixed modulus used to reduce are compile-time constants.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce): keep products unreduced in wide limbs and reduce once per accumulated expression, not per multiply. CAUTION: bellman-bignat [OWWB20] and similar bigint libraries are tuned for constraint DENSITY, not constraint COUNT — do not copy their limb layout without re-costing it against allocations+constraints.

mulmod as ONE polynomial-identity check at a single constant point (gnark/eprint 2025/933): hint quotient q and error/carry limbs e out of circuit, then enforce a(X)b(X) = c(X) + alpha(X)q(X) + (2^B - X)e(X) evaluated at ONE fixed X=2^B — collapses the full limb-by-limb equality into a single rank-1 product plus range checks on q,c,e, instead of one constraint per limb coefficient. Evaluate-at-a-point beats coefficient-matching in this R1CS metric; reuse the same hinted-then-checked shape for all 17 squarings/multiplies.

PKCS1v15 padding is almost entirely CONSTANT: the 0x00 01 FF...FF 00 prefix and the DigestInfo DER header are fixed bytes. Comparing the recovered padded block against them costs only affine equality checks against constants — allocate nothing for the padding bytes themselves, and never range-check a byte whose value is fixed by the spec.
secp256k1-scalar-mul: HEAD-TO-HEAD MODMUL COUNTS ACROSS FOUR CODEBASES, ALL COMPILED AND MEASURED IN OUR MODEL (no lookups, no challenges), for one 256-bit a*b mod p over BN254: jsnark/xJsnark with a CONSTANT modulus and lazy range = 623 constraints at 32-bit chunks; jsnark with a variable modulus = 637 at 26-bit; arkworks r1cs-std emulated_fp = 680 (66 for mul_without_reduce + 614 for reduce) at 17 limbs x 15 bits; gnark v0.8.1 = 724 at 26x10 and 888 at its shipped 64x4. LIMB WIDTH 26-32 LOOKED OPTIMAL AND 64 LOOKED 18-22% WORSE. THE RECORD IS STILL AT 4 LIMBS x 64 BITS, SO THIS LEVER IS UNCLAIMED — BUT THE TRADE HAS SHIFTED AND THE RE-MODEL MUST BE REDONE HONESTLY. With the pseudo-Mersenne quotient fold in place a multiply-subtract is 448/453, of which 95.8% is range-check bits: 508 for the result's canonicality, 141 for the 71-bit quotient, 214 for the 107-bit grouped carry. Narrower limbs shrink the carries but multiply the CELL COUNT (2m-1 grows) and, critically, blow up the table lookup: VarLookup goes 135 -> 255 per step, which is +7,440 across the loop and must be paid out of whatever the carries save. Re-cost against 448/453, NOT against the 728/735 that the original comparison assumed.

GLV DESIGN SPACE — CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT ARGUMENT (a subagent compiled real gnark circuits for secp256k1 emulated over BN254, PATCHING OUT gnark's lookup-based range checker so the numbers are in OUR model). Loop totals, plain R1CS: naive 256-bit ladder 958486; classic 2-dim GLV 452744; fake-GLV without endomorphism 452398; 4-dim GLV+fake-GLV at 66 bits 288019. THE 4-DIM CONSTRUCTION IS THE RIGHT ONE and the extra two lattice dimensions come from NON-DETERMINISTIC ADVICE, not from the curve: hint Q = [s]P and verify a relation, which makes the kernel lattice rank 4 with determinant n and all four coefficients about n^(1/4). GENERAL LAW, matching gnark-crypto's own documented bounds to within half a bit: allowing t points in the verified relation gives rank 2t, determinant n^(t-1), coefficients Theta(n^((t-1)/(2t))) — 1.15*sqrt(r) at t=1, 1.25*r^(1/4) at t=2, 1.28*r^(1/3) at t=3. CRUCIALLY THAT EXPONENT INCREASES WITH t, so beyond 4 dimensions the loop gets LONGER: measured 6-dim costs 370251 against 4-dim's 256287, plus about 80k more precomputation — a 70% loss. Per-iteration cost is nearly FLAT in dimension (3727/3810/4104 rows per iteration at 2/4/6 dims), so in-circuit cost is essentially iterations x constant and iterations = bit length. This is why the software result of eprint 2025/1151 (three scalars of a third the size, ~20% faster verification) DOES NOT TRANSFER to circuits, and why gnark ships the 6-dim variant only for NATIVE twisted Edwards with LogUp, never for emulated curves. Window size confirmed too: at 4 dims w=1 is the global optimum (256287) and w=2 loses badly (331953).

CORRECTION — A SIGN SELECT ON AN EMULATED POINT IS 4 ALLOCATIONS + 4 CONSTRAINTS, NOT ~599. I earlier costed the fake-GLV sign handling at about 599 rows for one emulated Select. In this cost model a mux over a 4-limb Emu value is literally 4 rows (one per limb), so the record's four sign selects total 16 allocations + 16 constraints. THE DESIGN RULE THAT MATTERS: mux only the SIGN-DEPENDENT part. Negating a point changes y and nothing else, so muxing a whole 9-cell FlaggedPoint wastes rows on x and isInf. The underlying advice — handle signs by negating the POINTS, never the scalars, and keep the loop free of sign work — stands and is what the record does.

MEASURED TARGET FOR THE MODMUL: 845 SCORE, AGAINST OUR 1463 (mulModSub2Cost = 728 alloc + 735 constr). These numbers come from actually compiling circuits with circom 2.2.3 and reading row counts out of the .r1cs with snarkjs, then witness-testing on 508 vectors including the worst case (p-1)^2 — not from a paper. Reference points, as rows + allocations: circom-ecdsa BigMultModP(64,4) = 7707; circom-pairing FpMultiply(43,6) at secp256k1 = 2509; fold with tightened carry parameters at n=32,k=8 = 1527; FOLD + CRT at n=32,k=8 = 845 (424 rows + 421 allocs). THREE INGREDIENTS, IN ORDER OF IMPORTANCE. (1) THE PRODUCT IS ALREADY FREE — the full 256x256 limb product is 2k-1 rows by asserting the limb-polynomial identity at 2k-1 evaluation points (circom-ecdsa's BigMultNoCarry is 7 rows), so 99.8% of a naive BigMultModP is carries and range checks and NO effort should go into the multiplication. (2) THE FOLD IS FREE FOR EVERY MODULUS — reducing the 2k-1 product limbs back to k via precomputed constants 2^(n(k+i)) mod p is a LINEAR COMBINATION, zero rows. What p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977 buys is that the fold coefficients are TINY (literally 977 and 1 when n = 32, because c = 2^32 + 977 is limb-aligned there), which cascades: folded limb width 77 bits instead of 101, quotient bound 36 bits instead of 68, CRT limbs 2 instead of 3, carry width 46 instead of 70 — worth about 27% (424 vs 578 rows for a generic 256-bit prime, both compiled). USE n = 32 PRECISELY BECAUSE c IS LIMB-ALIGNED THERE. (3) THE BIG ONE — CHECK THE IDENTITY BY CRT, NOT BY A CARRY CHAIN (Lubarov and Baylina, 'Casting out Primes', eprint 2022/1470): verify under a FIXED set of moduli M = {r_BN254, 2^(nT)} and conclude the identity holds mod lcm(M), which suffices when |f| < lcm(M). NOTE THIS NEEDS NO RANDOM CHALLENGE — the moduli are fixed constants, so it maps to plain R1CS. Mod r_BN254 the check R - p*X - out = 0 is ONE PURELY LINEAR ROW because the modulus is a CONSTANT; mod 2^(nT) only T = 2 carries at 46 bits are needed instead of a full chain of 8. Soundness margin measured at 25 bits (|D|max = 2^293 < r*2^64 = 2^318) and brute-forced on scaled-down analogues. CAVEAT FOR RSA: there the modulus is an INPUT, so p*X is a genuine product and the native leg is NOT free — this transfers to the secp challenges much better than to RSA.

SPARSE-PRIME CANONICITY IS 8 ALLOCATIONS + 11 CONSTRAINTS GIVEN THE BITS — MY EARLIER '37 ROWS' WAS 2x TOO HIGH. Comparing an already-decomposed 256-bit value against p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977 needs neither a subtraction nor a generic lexicographic comparator, because p's binary expansion has ONLY SIX ZERO BITS (positions 32, 9, 8, 7, 6, 4) and everything else is 1. So x < p iff some all-one run of p contains a zero of x, checked as a short prefix chain: (1) topEq <- IsZeroField(sum of deficit bits over positions 255..33), then one row topEq*b[32] = 0; (2) midEq <- IsZeroField(deficit over 31..10), throughMid <== topEq*midEq; (3) ONE row throughMid*(b[9]+b[8]+b[7]+b[6]) = 0 — four boolean bits sum below the native modulus, so one row enforces all four; (4) through5 <== throughMid*b[5]; (5) lowEq <- IsZeroField(deficit over 3..0), one row through5*(b[4] + lowEq) = 0. TOTAL 8 allocations / 11 constraints ON TOP of the decomposition = 19 score, against 260/265 for Normalize + LessThan. THE METHOD IS GENERIC: count the ZERO bits of the modulus, summarise each all-one run with one IsZeroField, chain the prefix-equality state with one product per run boundary — rows scale with the number of ZERO BITS of p, not with 256.

THE PSEUDO-MERSENNE QUOTIENT FOLD IS NOW IMPLEMENTED AND IT WAS THE WHOLE 36% CUT — MY EARLIER ESTIMATE UNDERSTATED IT. p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977, so 2^256 = cFold = 2^32 + 977, and the 7 product cells fold onto 4 by d_k = c_k + cFold*c_{k+4} — a FREE linear recombination because cFold is a compile-time constant. THE POINT IS WHAT THAT DOES TO THE QUOTIENT: instead of witnessing q as a 4-limb BigInt and paying a 252-row Normalize on it, q becomes ONE FIELD ELEMENT WITH A 71-BIT RANGE CHECK, and the carry chain collapses from 3 carries at 68 bits to ONE carry at 107 bits (grouped schedule L=6, groups [2,1,3], G=3). MEASURED: the target certificate goes 464/468 -> 184/186, so a multiply-subtract goes 728/735 -> 448/453 — 562 score per certificate, not the 316 I predicted. Across 350 live certificates that is 196,700, which is essentially the entire 559597 -> 355748 improvement. I also predicted GroupedEqXV would be 'a wash'; it is better than a wash. IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE: FoldParams / FoldTheorems.lhsVec+rhsVec / FoldTarget / MulModFold.

PER-STEP MULTIPLICATION COUNT IS AT THE FLOOR AND THE RECORD CONFIRMS IT — only the absolute numbers moved. Affine add is 3 certificates, generic double 4, triple 6, and the fused 2P+Q is 5 because it omits y of the intermediate. The record's FusedStep is now 2346 allocations / 2371 constraints (it was 3782 before the quotient fold) and is still EXACTLY 5 certificates: 3 multiply-subtracts at 448/453 and 2 fused divisions at 476/481. Those 5 certificates are 4617 of the step's 4717 score — 97.9%. CONSEQUENCE: per-step structural cleverness is spent; everything now rides on the cost of a single certificate, which is 95.8% range-check bits (508 for the result's canonicality, 141 for the 71-bit quotient, 214 for the 107-bit grouped carry).

CALIBRATION — OUR NUMBERS APPEAR TO BE THE ONLY PLAIN-R1CS ONES IN EXISTENCE. circom-ecdsa ECDSAVerifyNoPubkeyCheck(64,4) is 1508136 constraints and its fixed-base ECDSAPrivToPub is 95444 (stride 8, 32 windows, 256-entry tables); subtracting gives roughly 1.39-1.40M for its variable-base scalar multiplication. Against that our 559597 and 80147 are about 2.5x and 1.2x better. Everything smaller in the literature is out of scope: gnark's 100914 for [s]P uses logUp range checks plus a multicommit challenge; spartan-ecdsa's 3039 proves over secq256k1 where the field is NATIVE; halo2-ecc is PLONKish and lookup-driven. The one transferable idea from spartan-ecdsa is the efficient-ECDSA transform (two scalar multiplications down to one), which is R1CS-neutral and orthogonal to this challenge.

THE Y-FREE (x, lambda) LOOP IS 4 CERTIFICATES NOT 5 AND IS WORTH ~55k — BUT IT IS BLOCKED BY THE IDENTITY TABLE ENTRY, SO DO NOT ATTEMPT IT BEFORE RECODING. This replaces my earlier note that simply called it the biggest lever; the algebra is better than I said and the obstruction is one I had not seen. THE ALGEBRA WORKS, AND THE SAVING COMES FROM REUSING AN EXISTING CONSTRAINT. Our Slope2 already computes the halo2 quantity: its Spec asserts w*(xSe - rx) = 2*ry, i.e. 2y = w*(x_S - x). Stop treating that as the equation that DETERMINES w and treat it as the DEFINITION of y, and y/y' stop being witnesses. Four witnesses (lam1, x_S, w, x') and four constraints: (1) lam1*(t_x - x) = t_y - w*(x_S - x)/2; (2) x_S = lam1^2 - x - t_x; (3) x' = A^2 - x_S - x with A = lam1 + w free affine; (4) HANDOFF w'*(x_S' - x') + w*(x_S - x) = 2*A*(x' - x), which is the old y' = A(x'-x) - y with BOTH y's substituted — step i's from its own (w, x_S), step i+1's from ITS own (w', x_S'). Constraint (4) needs ZERO extra convolutions: its own is A*(x'-x), w*(x_S-x) is reused free from (1), and w'*(x_S'-x') free from step i+1. THE T-FORM PORT OF THE FIXED-BASE SIBLING IS THE WRONG DESIGN AND IS NEARLY WORTHLESS: anchoring the implied y to the last table point (y = lam*(u-x) - v) needs a FIFTH witness lam' — the chord slope of 2R and T — with its own certificate, giving 5 FRESH + 5 CERT + 2 convolutions = 2214/2239, a saving of only 84 per step.

MONTGOMERY-LADDER / x-ONLY IS THE WRONG DIRECTION HERE — DO NOT SPEND SLOTS ON IT. (a) secp256k1 has PRIME group order, hence no point of order 2 or 4, hence NO Montgomery form and no Edwards form over Fp — the classic Montgomery xz-ladder simply does not exist for this curve. (b) Brier-Joye x-only differential addition DOES work on any short Weierstrass curve, but its whole point is avoiding inversions, and in R1CS an inversion is ~1 allocation + 1 constraint (hint inv, enforce x*inv=1) — nearly free — so projective (X:Z) trades cheap inversions for extra non-native MULTIPLICATIONS, each ~730 rows (mulModSub2Cost 728/734). A 256-bit x-only ladder at ~10 field muls per bit is ~2560 mul-mods ~ 1.9M rows, versus 563079 for the current GLV+window circuit. The RIGHT reading of 'work on one coordinate' in this cost model is NOT a ladder but lambda-deferral: keep (x, lambda) through the loop and materialize y once (see the halo2 entry above).
GLV: decompose k = k1 + k2*lambda (mod n) into two ~128-bit halves; the endomorphism psi(x,y)=(beta*x mod p, y) costs ~6 constraints; then k*P = k1*P + k2*psi(P) halves the number of doublings.

GLV-3 / higher-dimensional decomposition (eprint 2025/1151, 2025/933): split k into THREE ~85-bit sub-scalars using the endomorphism twice (k = k0 + k1*lambda + k2*lambda^2 mod n); ~85 doublings instead of ~128, run as a joint 3-MSM sharing every doubling. Fewer doublings = fewer non-native Fp ops.

Find SHORTEST decomposition vectors via integer lattice reduction or a half-extended Euclidean algorithm in the endomorphism ring (eprint 2025/933); secp256k1's small CM discriminant (D=-3, j=0) admits extra reductions (reported 22-53% proving-time drop vs prior SOTA).
Run the decomposed halves/thirds as a width-w windowed joint-MSM (double-then-add) sharing doublings — reference figure ~2176 constraints for the 2-MSM core.
Per scalar bit the naive cost is ~4 (point selects) + ~4 (adds) + ~2 (double); wNAF / signed-digit windows cut the number of ADDITIONS via longer zero runs.

PRIME-REDUCE for a FIXED prime (circom-ecdsa): do limb mul/add WITHOUT carries into a wide form (k=4 x 64-bit registers for 256-bit; a product spans ~10 registers), then collapse 10 registers back to 4 in ONE reduction (~1000 constraints) by subtracting PRECOMPUTED multiples of p — compile-time constants because p is fixed. DEFERRAL BUDGET: keep 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < 254 (native field bits); that inequality tells you exactly how many unreduced products you may accumulate before a carry/reduce pass is actually required — defer right up to it, not further.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce, ~2x fewer reductions): accumulate a*b +/- c*d in WIDE UNREDUCED limbs and reduce ONCE at the end. Affine EC formulas are exactly this shape — lambda = (y2-y1)*inv(x2-x1), x3 = lambda^2 - x1 - x2, y3 = lambda*(x1-x3) - y1 — so reduce once PER OUTPUT COORDINATE, never per intermediate product.

COORDINATE-SYSTEM TRAP: in R1CS an inversion costs ~1 allocation + 1 constraint (hint inv as a witness, enforce x*inv = 1), so division is nearly FREE here — the opposite of the software cost model. Jacobian/projective/co-Z formulas (incl. Meloni co-Z ladders at ~11M+5S+23A per scalar bit) exist ONLY to avoid inversion, and pay for it with extra MULTIPLICATIONS — which are the expensive non-native op in-circuit. Prefer plain AFFINE add/double with hinted inverses; do NOT port inversion-free coordinate systems from the ECC literature.
Use INCOMPLETE / affine addition formulas (cheaper than complete-addition) where exceptional cases are ruled out by the decomposition, guarded by a soundness argument.

Precomputed-points-as-HINTS (eprint 2025/933): compute the scalar-mul result and per-step accumulator points OUTSIDE the circuit and pass them as witnesses; the circuit only CHECKS each group-law relation, which is cheaper than deriving points in-circuit. The prior R1CS baseline was ~9 constraints per scalar bit — beat that per bit.

AUDIT FOR OVER-ALLOCATION in the incomplete-add ladder (circom-ecdsa finding): only the first ~3 steps actually need the complete-addition guard, so accumulator/point arrays sized [bits] can be cut to [bits-3] and [3]. Allocations are HALF the cost metric here — sweep every witness array for entries that are never constrained or never read.

Non-native Fp: minimal-limb schoolbook mul + reduce with carry-save accumulation and top-bit-fold limb range checks; the flexible-limb EqViaCarries family (see reference/) may pack the equality check tighter.

THE EISENTRAEGER-LAUTER-MONTGOMERY RECASTING: COMPUTE [2]P + Q AS (P+Q)+P AND NEVER FORM y_R — 5 ROWS PER DOUBLE-AND-ADD STEP INSTEAD OF 7. Source: zcash/zcash issue #3924 ('Faster variable-base scalar multiplication in zk-SNARK circuits'), which claims 6 constraints/bit against a prior best of 8.5 with recoded scalars. WARNING, AND THIS IS WHY IT CANNOT BE COPIED VERBATIM: the equations in that issue are for a MONTGOMERY curve B*y^2 = x^3 + A*x^2 + x, and secp256k1 has PRIME ORDER so it has no Montgomery form at all (see the Montgomery-ladder do-not-try note). Only the RECASTING transfers. DERIVED AND VERIFIED HERE for short Weierstrass with a = 0: the point is that y_R of the intermediate R = P+Q is never needed, because lam2 = (y_R - y_P)/(x_R - x_P) simplifies to lam1 + lam2 = -2*y_P/(x_R - x_P). FIVE ROWS, five allocations: (1) (x_Q - x_P)*lam1 = y_Q - y_P; (2) lam1*lam1 = x_R + x_P + x_Q; (3) (x_R - x_P)*(lam1 + lam2) = -2*y_P; (4) lam2*lam2 = x_S + x_P + x_R; (5) (x_P - x_S)*lam2 = y_S + y_P. Against the naive route — double (x*x = xsq; (2y)*lam = 3*xsq + a; lam*lam = x2 + 2x; (x - x2)*lam = y2 + y, 4 rows) then add (3 rows) = 7 — that is 2 rows AND 2 allocations saved, i.e. 4 SCORE PER SCALAR BIT. VERIFIED: 39991/39991 exact matches against reference (P+Q)+P over a small curve with a = 0, every output on the curve. THE EXCEPTIONAL CASES ARE COMPLETELY CHARACTERIZED, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE GUARD CHEAP: exactly two rows can degenerate — row 1 when x_Q = x_P (i.e. Q = +-P), and row 3 when x_R = x_P, which happens IF AND ONLY IF Q = -2P (verified: every sampled degeneracy was exactly that). Nothing else can fail, so an exception guard needs those two tests and no more. HONEST RANKING AGAINST WHAT WE ALREADY HAVE: the halo2 'never witness y in the loop' note above is the STRONGER form — it carries (x_A, lam) and drops row 5 as well, so ELM is strictly an intermediate. Use ELM where a y-coordinate genuinely has to exist at that step (window boundaries, the final point), and halo2's ladder everywhere else.

SLOPE-ONLY TERMINAL ASSERTION — PROVING 2*A + T = O COSTS ONE SLOPE GADGET AND FOUR ROWS, NOT A DOUBLE-AND-ADD. When the last step of a scalar-mul or MSM only has to ASSERT that the accumulator chain closes to infinity, do not compute 2A+T and test the flag. Write S = A + T for the chord sum: the chord formula gives y_S = lambda*(x_A - x_S) - y_A, which collapses to -y_A exactly when x_S = x_A. So 2A + T = O <=> S = -A <=> x_S = x_A. A slope gadget already produces lambda and x_S = lambda^2 - x_A - x_T, so the whole assertion is ONE row A.isInf - T.isInf = 0 plus FOUR rows (1 - A.isInf)*(x_S[k] - x_A[k]) = 0. MEASURED (secp256k1 over BN254, 4 limbs x 64 bits): 1070 allocations / 1085 constraints, against 1792/1809 for double-then-cancel and 1783/1802 for assert-negated-sum — 722 allocations and 724 constraints saved, and being a pure assertion it materialises no output point. THE ONE SOUNDNESS OBLIGATION: the degenerate branch where x_T = x_A makes the slope gadget return the TANGENT, and you must show that branch cannot satisfy the assertion. For a = 0, b = 7 it forces lambda^2 = 3x together with 2*y*lambda = 3x^2, hence x^3 = -28 and y^2 = -21; -21 is a quadratic NON-RESIDUE mod p, proved by one kernel `decide` on a binary modPow at ZERO circuit rows. Re-derive the analogous non-residue before using this on another curve.

DO NOT ASSUME COMPLETE ADDITION IS EXPENSIVE — WITH LIMB-LEVEL MUXES IT IS 1.3% OF A STEP, AND THIS OVERTURNS THE USUAL ADVICE. The received wisdom (and my own earlier notes) says to use incomplete affine addition and discharge the exceptions by a soundness argument. MEASURED, THAT IS THE WRONG TRADE IN THIS COST MODEL: a FULLY COMPLETE fused double-add step is 2346 allocations / 2371 constraints, of which the entire exception apparatus is about 30 allocations — the other 97.9% is the five non-native certificates. The apparatus is two 9-cell point muxes (9/9 each) for A = O and T = -A, two 256-bit equality tests at 5/5, and one 2/2 opposite-y detector. THREE TRICKS MAKE IT THIS CHEAP. (1) 256-BIT EQUALITY IN 5 ROWS: pack limbs 0,1 into one native element and limbs 2,3 into another (each under 128 bits, safely below the native modulus), run two IsZeroField at 2/2, AND them with one row. DO NOT COMPARE LIMBWISE. (2) T = -A IN 2 ROWS USING ONE LIMB: witness inv of y_A[0] - y_T[0], set oppY <== yDiff*inv, assert yDiff*(sameX - oppY) = 0. Only the LOW LIMB is needed, because two finite points with equal x are equal or opposite and p is odd, so y != -y already differs in limb 0. (3) A BOOLEAN OR THAT COSTS ZERO: if one input IMPLIES the other (here T = O re-routes the intermediate x so sameX is forced to 1), the OR EQUALS the implied flag, and a downstream flag - other is a free affine expression instead of a witness plus a row. SO: reach for incomplete formulas only where a cheaper SPECIALISED gadget results — e.g. adding P to phi(P), where x_{phiP} != x_P is free from beta != 1 and x != 0, worth 63 allocations — and not to avoid completeness per se.

DEFERRED SUM-OF-EIGHT MOD-n CONGRUENCE IN 38 ALLOCATIONS / 44 CONSTRAINTS. The GLV scalar-side relation u1 + lambda*u2 + s*(v1 + lambda*v2) = 0 (mod n) decomposes into four mod-n products; DO NOT REDUCE THEIR SUM. Split each term by its sign into a positive and a negative bucket, bias the positive side by a constant 4n (free — n is a compile-time constant so 4n is a constant limb vector), witness a SINGLE quotient q, range-check it to THREE BITS (2 allocations / 3 constraints), and assert sum(positives) + 4n = sum(negatives) + q*n with ONE grouped-carry limb equality (35/41). TOTAL 38/44. Against reducing each partial sum mod n that is roughly a 4x saving on the tail of the decomposition proof, and it is why the whole scalar relation is 2932/2954 = 1.65% of a 355748-score circuit. THE BIAS CONSTANT IS THE DESIGN PARAMETER: choose it so every limb of the positive side stays non-negative and the quotient bound stays tiny — four signed terms each below n need 4n and give q < 8.

THE RECORD'S TOP-LEVEL SHAPE, FOR ORIENTATION (355748 = 176973 allocations + 178775 constraints, read from its own cost proofs). 4-dimensional FAKE GLV with the result WITNESSED, never computed: witness Q (9 cells, 0 constraints), validate it on-curve and canonical (1864/1895 — which ALSO emits the output bytes for free), witness four signed 64-bit coefficients (260 allocations) with booleanity (260 constraints), assert the mod-n scalar relation (2932/2954), build a 16-entry table of all subset sums of {+-P, +-phiP, +-Q, +-phiQ} (16881/17074), then run a 64-position 4-way interleaved MSM that ENDS IN AN ASSERTION that u1*P + u2*phiP + v1*Q + v2*phiQ = O (155027/156592). NO RECODING AT ALL — no NAF, no wNAF, no signed digits; plain binary magnitude with one sign bit per coefficient, and signs applied to the TABLE POINTS. Window width 1 per coefficient, interleaved 4-wide, so each position consumes a 4-bit nibble indexing the 16-entry table. THE LOOP IS 87.6% OF THE CIRCUIT and one step is 2481/2506 = VarLookup 135/135 (a 4-level mux tree of 15 9-cell point muxes) plus FusedStep 2346/2371. The coefficient bound 2^64 = n^(1/4) comes from a PIGEONHOLE argument, not a lattice algorithm: (2^64)^4 > n forces a collision, and the short-coefficient property is used in exactly one place — ruling out the u = v = 0 forgery.

WHY THE Y-FREE LOOP IS CURRENTLY UNSATISFIABLE, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS A DIFFERENT PROJECT. The invariant 2y = w*(x_S - x) defines y only when x_S != x. Slope2.main FORCES x_S = x whenever T = O — `let xSe <- Mux { selector := tIsInf, ifTrue := rx, ifFalse := xS }` — deliberately, to reach the tangent branch. AND T = O IS GENERIC, NOT ADVERSARIAL: GLVBuildTable.lean:124 proves `subsetPoint B 0 = .infinity`, i.e. TABLE ENTRY 0 IS THE POINT AT INFINITY, because the table is SUBSET sums with no recoding. Nibble 0000 selects it with probability 1/16 per position; over 62 interior steps the expected count is 3.9 and P(never) = (15/16)^62 = 1.8%. So on essentially every honest input the y-free system asserts 0 = 2y and THE CIRCUIT IS UNSATISFIABLE — a completeness failure, not a corner case. DROPPING THE CONSTRAINT INSTEAD IS A TOTAL SOUNDNESS BREAK: w unconstrained => A = lam1 + w unconstrained => x' unconstrained => the accumulator is steerable => the terminal `= O` assertion is free, and because fake-GLV WITNESSES Q the prover can engineer the collision at will. Halo2 is safe only because its base is fixed and public and its exclusion argument (Halo paper Thm 3 plus an integer index-shadow loop) runs over Z with one bounded scalar; our rank-4 lattice with witnessed Q and phiQ = lambda*Q admits no such argument. FOUR ESCAPES CHECKED, ALL CLOSED: (i) tangent from the implied y is w*w*(x_S-x) = 3x^2, DEGREE 3 — our interpolatedMul is a degree-2 convolution at 7 points with a 71-bit folded quotient, and a triple product needs 10 points and a ~512-bit quotient, dearer than the 531 saved; (ii) the T-form is non-degenerate at x_S = x but its tangent is still cubic in mu*lam*(u-x), and reducing it needs a witnessed pi = w*lam at 440/445 — exactly what was saved; (iii) a reciprocal state iota = 1/(2y) makes the tangent degree 2 but the CHORD cubic; (iv) an offset/blinding point making the table O-free needs Delta != -T_j for 16 adversarial T_j. THE PREREQUISITE IS THE ALL-ODD SIGNED-DIGIT RECODE (see the fixed-base sibling's free-recode entry, 0/0 cost) so that no nibble can select the identity. THREE INGREDIENTS, IN ORDER OF IMPORTANCE. (1) THE PRODUCT IS ALREADY FREE — the full 256x256 limb product is 2k-1 rows by asserting the limb-polynomial identity at 2k-1 evaluation points (circom-ecdsa's BigMultNoCarry is 7 rows), so 99.8% of a naive BigMultModP is carries and range checks and NO effort should go into the multiplication. (2) THE FOLD IS FREE FOR EVERY MODULUS — reducing the 2k-1 product limbs back to k via precomputed constants 2^(n(k+i)) mod p is a LINEAR COMBINATION, zero rows. What p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977 buys is that the fold coefficients are TINY (literally 977 and 1 when n = 32, because c = 2^32 + 977 is limb-aligned there), which cascades: folded limb width 77 bits instead of 101, quotient bound 36 bits instead of 68, CRT limbs 2 instead of 3, carry width 46 instead of 70 — worth about 27% (424 vs 578 rows for a generic 256-bit prime, both compiled). USE n = 32 PRECISELY BECAUSE c IS LIMB-ALIGNED THERE. (3) THE BIG ONE — CHECK THE IDENTITY BY CRT, NOT BY A CARRY CHAIN (Lubarov and Baylina, 'Casting out Primes', eprint 2022/1470): verify under a FIXED set of moduli M = {r_BN254, 2^(nT)} and conclude the identity holds mod lcm(M), which suffices when |f| < lcm(M). NOTE THIS NEEDS NO RANDOM CHALLENGE — the moduli are fixed constants, so it maps to plain R1CS. Mod r_BN254 the check R - p*X - out = 0 is ONE PURELY LINEAR ROW because the modulus is a CONSTANT; mod 2^(nT) only T = 2 carries at 46 bits are needed instead of a full chain of 8. Soundness margin measured at 25 bits (|D|max = 2^293 < r*2^64 = 2^318) and brute-forced on scaled-down analogues. CAVEAT FOR RSA: there the modulus is an INPUT, so p*X is a genuine product and the native leg is NOT free — this transfers to the secp challenges much better than to RSA.

SUPERSEDED — KEEP ONLY AS BACKGROUND. The halo2 fixed-base trick of offsetting window w's table by a constant so no window can select the identity is real, but the all-odd signed-digit recode (see the free-recode entry) achieves the same guarantee AND halves every table AND needs no last-window correction term. Use the recode, not the offset.

Base G is FIXED: every window multiple j*(2^{w*i})*G is a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT — bake the whole comb table into the circuit as constants (zero constraints to build it), unlike the variable-base case.
Comb method: k = sum b_{i} 2^{i}; group bits into d combs of width w so each step is ONE table select + ONE add; fewer adds than plain windowed double-and-add.
Width-w NAF / signed-digit recoding of the scalar so table entries cover +/- multiples, halving table size and generating more zero (skip) positions.

Signed-digit tables cost almost nothing to apply: -P = (x, -y), so the sign bit drives ONE modular negation of y (an affine op), NOT a second multiplexer. So a width-w signed table needs only 2^{w-1} constant entries selected, plus a conditional y-negation — half the select cost of an unsigned width-w table for the same window count.
Constant-table point selection as a multiplexer over field constants: select cost is linear in window size but touches only additions/booleans, no non-native mul.

PRIME-REDUCE for a FIXED prime (circom-ecdsa): do limb mul/add WITHOUT carries into a wide form (k=4 x 64-bit registers for 256-bit; a product spans ~10 registers), then collapse 10 registers back to 4 in ONE reduction (~1000 constraints) by subtracting PRECOMPUTED multiples of p — compile-time constants because p is fixed. DEFERRAL BUDGET: keep 3n + log2(2k^2) + eps < 254 (native field bits); that inequality tells you exactly how many unreduced products you may accumulate before a carry/reduce pass is actually required — defer right up to it, not further.

SUM-OF-PRODUCTS, ONE REDUCTION (arkworks nonnative mul_without_reduce, ~2x fewer reductions): accumulate a*b +/- c*d in WIDE UNREDUCED limbs and reduce ONCE at the end. Affine EC formulas are exactly this shape — lambda = (y2-y1)*inv(x2-x1), x3 = lambda^2 - x1 - x2, y3 = lambda*(x1-x3) - y1 — so reduce once PER OUTPUT COORDINATE, never per intermediate product.

COORDINATE-SYSTEM TRAP: in R1CS an inversion costs ~1 allocation + 1 constraint (hint inv as a witness, enforce x*inv = 1), so division is nearly FREE here — the opposite of the software cost model. Jacobian/projective/co-Z formulas (incl. Meloni co-Z ladders at ~11M+5S+23A per scalar bit) exist ONLY to avoid inversion, and pay for it with extra MULTIPLICATIONS — which are the expensive non-native op in-circuit. Prefer plain AFFINE add/double with hinted inverses; do NOT port inversion-free coordinate systems from the ECC literature.

Combine comb sub-scalars as a joint accumulation sharing point doublings/additions (multi-comb), analogous to the joint-MSM trick, so the fixed precompute is amortized across all windows in one add-chain.

Port secp256k1-scalar-mul's GroupedEqXV / MulModTarget non-native machinery (see reference/) if it lowers the per-add Fp mul-mod cost below the current Flex path; competitor csko pushed this challenge to 90041, a large structural gap — a comb-table + incomplete-add rewrite is likely needed, not incremental tweaks.

GLV IS STRICTLY BETTER ON A FIXED BASE — and is missing from this solution's playbook. Decompose k = k1 + k2*lambda (mod n) into two ~128-bit halves. Because the base is FIXED, lambda*G is itself a COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT: unlike the variable-base case there is NO in-circuit endomorphism to evaluate (variable-base pays ~6 constraints for psi(x,y)=(beta*x, y); here it costs ZERO). You get TWO constant comb tables (multiples of G and of lambda*G), both free to build, and run them as a JOINT accumulation sharing every doubling — roughly halving the add/double chain. The only in-circuit cost is checking the decomposition: k1 + k2*lambda = k (mod n) plus range checks on k1,k2 — one non-native relation, not per-bit work.

Push the same idea further: with all tables being compile-time constants there is no table-size penalty for HIGHER-DIMENSIONAL decomposition (GLV-3 via lambda^2, or 4-dimensional GLV). Each extra dimension shortens the sub-scalars (256 -> ~128 -> ~85 -> ~64 bits) and shortens the shared doubling chain proportionally, at the cost only of more CONSTANT tables (free) and a slightly bigger decomposition check. Sweep the dimension and pick the minimum of (doublings + selects + decomposition check).

mLSB-set comb is the standard pairing of comb methods with GLV curves (see the fixed-base comb / GLV-GLS literature) — combine mLSB-set recoding with the two (or more) constant tables rather than treating comb and GLV as alternatives.

SLOPE-ONLY TERMINAL ASSERTION — PROVING 2*A + T = O COSTS ONE SLOPE GADGET AND FOUR ROWS, NOT A DOUBLE-AND-ADD. When the last step of a scalar-mul or MSM only has to ASSERT that the accumulator chain closes to infinity, do not compute 2A+T and test the flag. Write S = A + T for the chord sum: the chord formula gives y_S = lambda*(x_A - x_S) - y_A, which collapses to -y_A exactly when x_S = x_A. So 2A + T = O <=> S = -A <=> x_S = x_A. A slope gadget already produces lambda and x_S = lambda^2 - x_A - x_T, so the whole assertion is ONE row A.isInf - T.isInf = 0 plus FOUR rows (1 - A.isInf)*(x_S[k] - x_A[k]) = 0. MEASURED (secp256k1 over BN254, 4 limbs x 64 bits): 1070 allocations / 1085 constraints, against 1792/1809 for double-then-cancel and 1783/1802 for assert-negated-sum — 722 allocations and 724 constraints saved, and being a pure assertion it materialises no output point. THE ONE SOUNDNESS OBLIGATION: the degenerate branch where x_T = x_A makes the slope gadget return the TANGENT, and you must show that branch cannot satisfy the assertion. For a = 0, b = 7 it forces lambda^2 = 3x together with 2*y*lambda = 3x^2, hence x^3 = -28 and y^2 = -21; -21 is a quadratic NON-RESIDUE mod p, proved by one kernel `decide` on a binary modPow at ZERO circuit rows. Re-derive the analogous non-residue before using this on another curve.

DO NOT ASSUME COMPLETE ADDITION IS EXPENSIVE — WITH LIMB-LEVEL MUXES IT IS 1.3% OF A STEP, AND THIS OVERTURNS THE USUAL ADVICE. The received wisdom (and my own earlier notes) says to use incomplete affine addition and discharge the exceptions by a soundness argument. MEASURED, THAT IS THE WRONG TRADE IN THIS COST MODEL: a FULLY COMPLETE fused double-add step is 2346 allocations / 2371 constraints, of which the entire exception apparatus is about 30 allocations — the other 97.9% is the five non-native certificates. The apparatus is two 9-cell point muxes (9/9 each) for A = O and T = -A, two 256-bit equality tests at 5/5, and one 2/2 opposite-y detector. THREE TRICKS MAKE IT THIS CHEAP. (1) 256-BIT EQUALITY IN 5 ROWS: pack limbs 0,1 into one native element and limbs 2,3 into another (each under 128 bits, safely below the native modulus), run two IsZeroField at 2/2, AND them with one row. DO NOT COMPARE LIMBWISE. (2) T = -A IN 2 ROWS USING ONE LIMB: witness inv of y_A[0] - y_T[0], set oppY <== yDiff*inv, assert yDiff*(sameX - oppY) = 0. Only the LOW LIMB is needed, because two finite points with equal x are equal or opposite and p is odd, so y != -y already differs in limb 0. (3) A BOOLEAN OR THAT COSTS ZERO: if one input IMPLIES the other (here T = O re-routes the intermediate x so sameX is forced to 1), the OR EQUALS the implied flag, and a downstream flag - other is a free affine expression instead of a witness plus a row. SO: reach for incomplete formulas only where a cheaper SPECIALISED gadget results — e.g. adding P to phi(P), where x_{phiP} != x_P is free from beta != 1 and x != 0, worth 63 allocations — and not to avoid completeness per se.

THE ALL-ODD SIGNED-DIGIT RECODE COSTS EXACTLY ZERO ROWS, AND THE SCALAR'S PARITY IS ABSORBED BY THE TOP WINDOW'S CONSTANT TABLE. Do not build a recoder. With MSB-first input bits, define db[c] := bits[254 - c] for c < 255 and db[255] := 1 — a pure WIRE PERMUTATION with one hard-coded 1, cost 0/0. Grouping db into W windows of w bits gives digits d_i = 2*v_i + 1 - 2^w, all ODD and in +-{1, 3, ..., 2^w - 1}, and the identity sum_i d_i * 2^(w*i) = k + 1 - bits[255] holds. THE PARITY FIX IS FREE: the comb computes k*G when the scalar is odd and (k+1)*G when even, and the -+G correction is folded into the TOP window's table by making the scalar's LSB an extra INDEX BIT of that table — a 16-entry 4-bit top table costs 11 rows whether or not the parity bit is in the index, so the fix costs NOTHING. WHAT THIS BUYS, AND IT IS THE WHOLE EXCEPTION STORY: every digit is odd hence nonzero, so no window can ever select the identity, and no two consecutive sites can collide — which is what lets the entire ladder use incomplete addition with no runtime guard except the 44-score final screen. SECOND BENEFIT: the magnitude index of a NEGATIVE digit is the bitwise COMPLEMENT of the magnitude bits, obtained as XNOR(sign, b_i) at ONE multiplication per bit (11 for w = 12), so the sign costs 11 rows and no separate table.

WHY IT IS THE RIGHT TOOL: in a multi-operand column-compression adder, each column's outputs are SYMMETRIC functions of that column's input bits (elementary symmetric Sigma^n_k and counting functions E^n_k), so this paper's tables are a direct lookup for the exact per-column cost, replacing the full-adder-tree assumption. WHAT IS NEW BEYOND Boyar-Peralta 2008: (a) ARITY-BASED HW-ENCODINGS that use full adders (H_FA) in place of the standard Hamming-weight method, cutting AND gates in phase 1; (b) DEGREE-BASED ENCODINGS that skip work for functions of degree < n; (c) FREE TRUTH-TABLE ENTRIES exploited by concatenation in phase 2. CONCRETE, AND THESE ANSWER TWO OPEN 2008 QUESTIONS: MC(Sigma^8_4) = MC(E^8_4) = 6 — strictly below the 8 - hw(8) = 7 that the Hamming-weight method charges for the full weight. Generally every symmetric function on n <= 25 variables has MC <= n - 1 (n = 22 is the lone exception at <= 22). HOW TO USE IT: the standing bound MC(Hamming weight of n bits) = n - hw(n) is for the FULL weight vector; when the adder only needs SOME output bits of a column, look the individual function up in these tables instead — Sigma^8_4 at 6 vs 7 is exactly that gap. This is the concrete handle on the one piece of unclaimed ground (joint MC of multi-operand modular addition): build the column compressor from per-column table lookups, not from a generic full-adder tree.

There is a large and still-active literature on minimizing the number of 2-input XOR gates needed to evaluate an F2-LINEAR MAP — the Shortest Linear Program problem: Boyar-Peralta, Tan-Peyrin (TCHES'20) adding randomization and 3-input XOR gates, the 'Superior Boyar-Peralta' (SBP) depth-aware heuristic, 'Improved Heuristics for Low-Latency Implementations of Linear Layers', and eprint 2025/1493 which revisits BP and cuts the AES linear layer from 91 to 89 g-XOR. IT IS NOT, BECAUSE AN XOR GATE COSTS NOTHING IN EITHER OF OUR COST MODELS. In native R1CS an affine combination lives inside the A/B/C vectors of a row and is free. In the GF(2) challenges the harness restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A and B AFFINE, so an arbitrary XOR-combination is free inside a multiplicand. Halving the XOR count of theta changes the score by ZERO. THEREFORE THE ONLY QUESTION WORTH ASKING IS: for each currently-materialized intermediate, WHO CONSUMES IT, and can that consumer take an affine form instead? Every row saved comes from deleting a materialization, never from restructuring the XOR tree that feeds it.

Do not spend a job porting it. Cross-check of the identity: record 44430 = 2 x 22215 ANDs; gf2-k12 baseline 38400 = 2 x 12 x 1600. This variant is PURELY an AND-count problem; nothing outside multiplicative complexity can move the score.

CALIBRATION AGAINST THE BEST PUBLISHED BOOLEAN CIRCUIT (Bristol Fashion sha256, nigelsmart.github.io/MPC-Circuits): that circuit computes EXACTLY this function — one compression call, buffer + chaining state -> next chaining state — in 22573 AND gates (110644 XOR, 1856 INV, total 135073, AND-depth 1607). Over GF(2) an AND is 1 allocation + 1 constraint (confirmed by the k12 baseline 1600 bits x 12 rounds x 2 = 38400), so the record is (score / 2) ANDs — at 44436 that is 22218, already ~355 BELOW the best-known hand-optimized Boolean circuit. Read that as: this challenge is at state-of-the-art in AND-count terms, generic 'reduce the ANDs' restructuring will NOT find easy wins, and any further gain must come from joint Boyar-Peralta-style minimization of the ADDER carry chains (~17-18k of the ANDs are carries; Ch+Maj are only 2 x 32 x 64 = 4096). Measure your candidate in ANDs and compare to (current seed score / 2) before believing it is an improvement; recompute that ratio from YOUR seed rather than trusting a number quoted here, since the record keeps moving.

GF(2): bits are free of booleanity; XOR/rotate/shift are FREE affine combinations. Cost concentrates in (a) AND gates in Ch/Maj and (b) the mod-2^32 ADDITION carry chains, which are NOT linear over GF(2) and usually dominate.

Minimum-AND forms: Ch(e,f,g) = g + e*(f+g) is ONE multiplication. Maj IS ALSO ONE, not two — Maj(a,b,c) = c + (a+c)*(b+c), since (a+c)(b+c) = ab+ac+bc+c over GF(2) (c^2 = c). The factored form a*b + c*(a+b) costs TWO and the symmetric ab+ac+bc costs three; use the (a+c)(b+c) version everywhere. This is the same identity as the full-adder carry maj(a,b,cin), so Maj and every carry bit cost exactly one multiplication each. Maj appears 32 x 64 = 2048 times, so paying two instead of one wastes up to 2048 ANDs = 4096 score.

CORRECTION — CARRY-SAVE IS NOT A WIN OVER GF(2): a full-adder carry is maj(a,b,cin) = ab + cin(a+b) = ONE multiplication, so a 32-bit mod-2^32 addition costs 31 muls (carries c_1..c_31), and a 3:2 compressor row ALSO costs 31. Reducing k addends therefore costs (k-1)*31 either way — carry-save buys DEPTH, not AND-count. Its advantage in large-field R1CS comes from avoiding range checks, which do not exist here. Do NOT restructure the adder tree expecting a win; the lever is FEWER ADDITIONS and SHARED carry subexpressions, not a different tree shape.

A full-adder carry over GF(2) is maj(a,b,cin) = ab + cin(a+b) — ONE multiplication; the sum bit a+b+cin is free. So a 32-bit ripple costs ~32 muls, and a 3:2 compressor costs 32 muls while removing an entire addend.

Baseline 95904 vs record 44784 — a >2x gap, so the record is NOT using a naive per-addend ripple. Assume a carry-save tree plus minimum-AND Ch/Maj, and look for further sharing of carry subexpressions across the 64 rounds.

Reference point: Flock's pinned SHA-256 R1CS encoder is 30,632 allocations + 30,632 constraints = 61,264 interface-normalized — already beaten by the 44784 record, so treat 61k as a floor to clear, not a goal.

MC FLOOR ARITHMETIC (Boyar-Peralta full-adder/half-adder optimality): count the mandatory multiplications. Per round T1 = h+Sigma1(e)+Ch+K+W is 4 adds = 124, Ch = 32, T2 = Sigma0(a)+Maj is 1 add = 31, Maj = 64, a=T1+T2 = 31, e=d+T1 = 31 -> ~313 muls/round x 64 = ~20.0k; message schedule 3 adds x 31 x 48 = ~4.5k; final 8-word add = 248. Naive total ~24.7k muls -> score ~49.5k. The record is 44780, BELOW that — so the record IS sharing work across rounds. Find the sharing; the adder shape alone will not get you there.

Where the sharing must be: (a) Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1 are free affine rotations — never allocate them; (b) K_t is a CONSTANT so h+K_t is affine, folding one whole addend out of T1's chain; (c) adding a constant costs FEWER than 31 muls because carries into known-zero constant bits are determined — specialize the adder per round constant instead of using a generic 32-bit adder; (d) reuse carry bits between the T1 chain and the e=d+T1 / a=T1+T2 adds where operands coincide.

OPTIMAL COUNTERS BEAT FULL-ADDER CHAINS (Boyar-Peralta, 'The Exact Multiplicative Complexity of the Hamming Weight Function'): MC of the Hamming weight of n bits is EXACTLY n - H(n), where H(n) is the Hamming weight of n's binary representation. Multi-operand addition is column-wise Hamming-weight counting, so a k:log(k) COUNTER is the right primitive, not a chain of 3:2 full adders. Check: k=3 gives 3-H(3)=1 (a full adder, 1 AND — consistent); k=7 gives 7-H(7)=4 ANDs for a 7:3 counter, strictly better than chaining full adders over the same 7 bits. SHA-256 sums 5 addends in T1 plus incoming carries, so columns are 5-7 bits deep — build OPTIMAL COUNTERS per column and let carries propagate between columns, rather than adding operands two at a time. This is the standard AND-minimisation technique and is the most likely source of the large structural drops competitors are landing.

THE RECORD IS ALREADY BELOW EVERY PUBLIC NETLIST, AND THE GAP IS FULLY ACCOUNTED FOR — so stop looking for a circuit to steal. EVERY PER-ADDER BOUND IS ALREADY TIGHT, AND AUTOMATED MC SYNTHESIS LOSES BY 20% — two closed doors, stated so no job wastes itself on them. (a) MC(n-bit addition mod 2^n) = n-1 EXACTLY: ripple achieves n-1, and the degree bound MC >= deg-1 forces >= n-1 because the ANF of c_{n-2} contains a0*b0*prod(a_l + b_l) (Boyar-Peralta, TCS 2008; cited by Testa et al. as '32-bit adder = 32 AND is known to be optimum'). (b) MC(Hamming weight of n bits) = n - H(n), achieved by full-adder trees, so column compression is already optimal. (c) Carry-save/Wallace for k operands mod 2^n costs (k-1)(n-1) — IDENTICAL to sequential ripple, not better; column-counter variants are WORSE (5 operands: 4 ANDs/column x 32 = 128 > 124). (d) Testa-Soeken-Amaru-De Micheli (EPFL mockturtle) ran the best published automated XAG MC flow on SHA-256: DAC'19 Table 2 got 89478 -> 30201, DATE'20 Table II with rewriting/refactoring/resubstitution to convergence got 26927 — i.e. 19% WORSE than the hand-built fixed-IV circuit, and 21% worse than the record.

THE ONE PIECE OF GENUINELY UNCLAIMED GROUND: THE *JOINT* MC OF MULTI-OPERAND MODULAR ADDITION. Every bound above is per-adder. Nobody has proved anything about adding k operands mod 2^32 in one shot. Boyar-Find (arXiv:1407.6169) does not treat adders at all and their best general (n,n) lower bound is 2n-3; the degree bound only forces about 31 against a construction costing (k-1)(n-1). CONCRETE TARGETS: a 5-operand 32-bit mod-2^32 adder below 124 ANDs, or a 4-operand below 93. LEVERAGE: the round sum T1 = h + Sigma1(e) + Ch + K_t + W_t is a 5-operand add that occurs 64 times, so any saving of D is worth 64D ANDs = 128D score; the schedule sum is a 4-operand add occurring 48 times, worth 48D' ANDs. Attack it as a single Boolean function of 5x32 inputs -> 32 outputs, not as a chain: look for shared carry subexpressions ACROSS operands (the carries of a+b and of c+d both consume the same column parities), and for the fact that only the final 32 sum bits are needed — all intermediate carries are internal and may be re-encoded freely.

AN EXPERIMENT THAT HAS DEMONSTRABLY NEVER BEEN RUN: seed mockturtle's MC-minimization flow FROM the 22573 (or the record's 22215) netlist rather than from an ABC 2-LUT baseline. Every published run starts from the LUT baseline, which is why they land at 26927. The same flow, on a HAND-CRAFTED Bristol circuit, cut DES 18124 -> 15093 (-17%) — so it can improve human work, it just was never pointed at this one. The output of the flow is an XAG, which IS exactly this challenge's cost model (AND count), so the result is directly importable with no translation loss. github.com/lsils/mockturtle. Expected yield low, cost low, and it is purely Boolean — no Lean proof burden until something is found.

CONCRETE MC TABLES FOR EVERY SYMMETRIC BOOLEAN FUNCTION UP TO 25 VARIABLES — the missing tool for the multi-operand-adder lever. Brandao, Calik, Sonmez Turan & Peralta, 'Upper Bounds on the Multiplicative Complexity of Symmetric Boolean Functions', eprint 2019/708. WHY IT IS THE RIGHT TOOL: in a multi-operand column-compression adder, each column's outputs are SYMMETRIC functions of that column's input bits (elementary symmetric Sigma^n_k and counting functions E^n_k), so this paper's tables are a direct lookup for the exact per-column cost, replacing the full-adder-tree assumption. WHAT IS NEW BEYOND Boyar-Peralta 2008: (a) ARITY-BASED HW-ENCODINGS that use full adders (H_FA) in place of the standard Hamming-weight method, cutting AND gates in phase 1; (b) DEGREE-BASED ENCODINGS that skip work for functions of degree < n; (c) FREE TRUTH-TABLE ENTRIES exploited by concatenation in phase 2. CONCRETE, AND THESE ANSWER TWO OPEN 2008 QUESTIONS: MC(Sigma^8_4) = MC(E^8_4) = 6 — strictly below the 8 - hw(8) = 7 that the Hamming-weight method charges for the full weight. Generally every symmetric function on n <= 25 variables has MC <= n - 1 (n = 22 is the lone exception at <= 22). HOW TO USE IT: the standing bound MC(Hamming weight of n bits) = n - hw(n) is for the FULL weight vector; when the adder only needs SOME output bits of a column, look the individual function up in these tables instead — Sigma^8_4 at 6 vs 7 is exactly that gap. This is the concrete handle on the one piece of unclaimed ground (joint MC of multi-operand modular addition): build the column compressor from per-column table lookups, not from a generic full-adder tree.

DO-NOT-TRY, AND IT IS A TEMPTING ONE: XOR-GATE / SHORTEST-LINEAR-PROGRAM MINIMIZATION BUYS EXACTLY ZERO HERE. There is a large and still-active literature on minimizing the number of 2-input XOR gates needed to evaluate an F2-LINEAR MAP — the Shortest Linear Program problem: Boyar-Peralta, Tan-Peyrin (TCHES'20) adding randomization and 3-input XOR gates, the 'Superior Boyar-Peralta' (SBP) depth-aware heuristic, 'Improved Heuristics for Low-Latency Implementations of Linear Layers', and eprint 2025/1493 which revisits BP and cuts the AES linear layer from 91 to 89 g-XOR. Keccak's theta (and rho/pi, and SHA-256's Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1) are exactly such linear maps, so this looks like the obvious attack on the biggest remaining slack. IT IS NOT, BECAUSE AN XOR GATE COSTS NOTHING IN EITHER OF OUR COST MODELS. In native R1CS an affine combination lives inside the A/B/C vectors of a row and is free. In the GF(2) challenges the harness restricts every row to `var k - A*B` with A and B AFFINE, so an arbitrary XOR-combination is free inside a multiplicand. Halving the XOR count of theta changes the score by ZERO. WHAT THETA'S 2240 ROWS PER ROUND ACTUALLY PAY FOR IS *MATERIALIZATION*, NOT XOR COUNT: a value costs an allocation exactly when it must appear as a BARE WITNESS VARIABLE — because it is a circuit output, or because its consumer needs a variable rather than an affine form. THEREFORE THE ONLY QUESTION WORTH ASKING IS: for each currently-materialized intermediate, WHO CONSUMES IT, and can that consumer take an affine form instead? Every row saved comes from deleting a materialization, never from restructuring the XOR tree that feeds it.

CROSS-ROUND CONJUGATION IS THE ONE MECHANISM THAT COULD BEAT A PER-ROUND MC FLOOR — AND IT APPLIES HERE TOO. Akpaki & David, 'Reducing Multiplicative Complexity via Conjugate Cipher', IACR eprint 2026/1365 (2026-07-02): replace the round F by a conjugate F' = C o F o C^-1 so that F^r = C^-1 o (F')^r o C and the conjugation is paid TWICE rather than r times. Reported 5.5% on Skinny64 and 3% on Skinny128, against best-known implementations rather than against a proven floor. WHY IT MATTERS FOR AN ITERATED COMPRESSION FUNCTION: every per-round MC bound we have — including the proved MC(chi_5) = 5 and the per-adder bounds for SHA-256 — is a bound on the round IN ISOLATION, and conjugation is precisely a way to never compute the real intermediate state. SHA-256's compression is 64 iterations of one round function, so it is a candidate. CAVEATS: the paper does not mention SHA-256 or Keccak; a NONLINEAR C is required (an affine C changes nothing); and the full PDF is Cloudflare-403 from this environment and absent from the Wayback Machine, so only the abstract is verified. Worth obtaining manually before spending a job on it.
